cards.text: The Magi have gone home another way. Then an angel of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph, Mary's husband. And friend, this angel did NOT come for small talk.

cards.question: The angel tells Joseph to take the Child and His mother and flee. Where to?

cards.text: Egypt it is, and the angel adds, "Stay there until I tell you". No end date, no "back by Friday," just stay until further notice.

cards.question: The angel tells Joseph that Herod is going to search for the Child so he can worship Him.

cards.text: Did you catch the angel's first words? "Get up!" Friend, if somebody said that to ME in my sleep, I'd be begging for five more minutes. Ten if I'm feeling brave.

cards.question: Joseph takes the Child and His mother and leaves for Egypt. When does he go?

cards.text: No five more minutes for this man. Joseph gets up and goes, and the family stays in Egypt until the death of Herod.

cards.question: Matthew says this fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: "Out of ___ I called My Son."

cards.text: Remember, Herod told the Magi to come back and report to him. Those Magi went home another way.

cards.question: Herod sees that the Magi outwitted him, and he is filled with ___.

cards.text: Herod sends out orders. He uses the exact time of the star that he learned from the Magi.

cards.question: Herod has boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity put to death. Which boys?

answers.text: Boys two years old and under
Boys one year old and under
Boys five years old and under

cards.text: This is a heartbreaking moment, friend. Matthew says it fulfilled the words of the prophet Jeremiah: a voice is heard in Ramah, and it's Rachel, Jacob's wife from long ago, weeping for her children.

cards.question: In Jeremiah's words, Rachel lets herself be comforted, even though her children are no more.

cards.text: Then Herod dies. Over in Egypt, an angel of the Lord appears to Joseph in a dream again. And you already know the first words: "Get up!"

cards.question: The angel says, "Take the Child and His mother and go to the land of ___"
Why can Joseph bring the Child back now, according to the angel?

answers.text: Those seeking the Child's life are dead
Egypt is no longer safe for them
The people of Israel are asking for Him

cards.text: So Joseph gets up and goes to the land of Israel with the Child and His mother. Two "Get up!"s, zero requests for five more minutes, and me? I lose arguments with my own oven timer.
But then Joseph learns that Archelaus is reigning in Judea in place of his father Herod.

cards.question: Archelaus, Herod's son, is now reigning in Judea. How does Joseph feel about going there?
Before Joseph withdraws to the district of Galilee, he is warned in a dream.
In Galilee, Joseph goes and lives in a town called ___.

cards.text: So was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophets: "He will be called a Nazarene." From a night escape to Egypt all the way to a hometown in Nazareth, friend, and every move came from a dream showing Joseph the way.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "Out of ___ I called My Son.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 2 quotes "Take the Child and His mother and go to the land of ___", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card goes back to the angel's first words, "Get up!", from Matthew 2:13. Cards 2 through 4 already moved past that verse. The card only sets up a joke and does not move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "After three days" is a delay, while "By night" and "At sunrise" are times of day. That makes it a different kind of answer from the other two.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card cites Matthew 2:16, but none of its content comes from that verse. Herod telling the Magi to report back is Matthew 2:8, and the Magi going home another way is Matthew 2:12. Both are outside the passage. The card also recaps the previous passage, and card 1 already said the Magi went home another way.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't map to the moment. The core action is getting up and obeying right away, with no delay. Losing arguments with an oven timer is a different action, so the line reads as a "huh?". This is also the third time the "five more minutes" bit is used.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card says "every move came from a dream showing Joseph the way." That isn't true to the text. In Matthew 2:22, Joseph learns about Archelaus and is afraid. Matthew 2:23 never says a dream sent him to Nazareth. The closing line is also a recap of the whole passage.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's humor is thin and repeats itself. Apart from "did NOT come for small talk" and "back by Friday," almost every joke is the same "five more minutes" bit (stop 1 cards 5 and 7, stop 2 card 4). Several story cards read as plain narration with little voice: stop 1 card 9 and stop 2 card 5. Stop 1 cards 11 to 14 cover the killing of the boys, so keeping those cards quiet is right.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem:
Several cards state facts from outside the passage without a reference:
- Stop 1 card 1: the Magi going home another way (Matt 2:12) and Joseph as Mary's husband (Matt 1:16).
- Stop 1 card 11: "the exact time of the star" (Matt 2:7). Matthew 2:16 only says "the time he had learned from the Magi."
- Stop 1 card 13: Rachel as Jacob's wife (Gen 29:28).

prep-walkthrough.md says outside facts need "their reference." But a card's "verses" field can only cite the verses the card tells, and papa-dorin.md's new-person example ("Cyrus, king of Persia") has no reference.
findings.question: When a card uses a fact from outside the passage, how should its reference be given? Options include inside the card's text, in an extra field, or not at all for short introductions of who a new person is.
